carousels.name: 3 things an 82,243-person study says about p*rn addiction

slides.title: 3 things an 82,243-person study says [[about p*rn addiction.]]
slides.sub: 42 countries. One of the biggest studies ever done on it.

slides.title: It's [[real]] and common
slides.body: Depending on the measure, 3.2%–16.6% of people were at risk of problematic p*rn use. That's millions of people worldwide.

slides.title: Men are [[most]] affected
slides.body: Men reported the highest levels of problematic p*rn use, followed by gender-diverse people and women. But anyone can struggle.

slides.title: Few get [[help]]
slides.body: Only 4–10% of people with problematic use had ever sought treatment. Most people deal with it alone.

slides.title: Don't be a [[statistic]]
items: Take it seriously — it's a recognised problem.
Ask for professional help if you need it.
slides.note: Send this to someone who thinks they're the only one ↗

slides.title: 6 phone rules couples make [[when one of them is quitting p*rn.]]
Rules [[1–2]]
items: No phones at dinner — real time together.

slides.title: Rules [[3–4]]
items: Open passcodes — if you both agree, not as punishment.

slides.title: Rules [[5–6]]
items: Blockers on every device — his idea, his setup.
Weekly check-in about how p*rn recovery is going.

slides.title: Rules work [[when they're shared]]
slides.body: If one person sets the rules, it turns into policing. Agree on them together — and change them as trust grows back after p*rn.

carousels.name: 5 rules for the final 72 hours of NNN

slides.title: 5 rules for the final 72 hours [[of No Nut November without p*rn.]]
slides.sub: 3 days left. Don't get clever now.

slides.title: Rules [[1–2]]
items: No "just checking." No old accounts, no p*rn searches.

slides.title: Rules [[3–4]]
items: One check-in a day with someone you trust.

slides.title: Bed by [[midnight]]
slides.body: Every relapse story seems to have a late night in it. Three early nights. That's all.

slides.title: After [[72 hours]]
items: Set a new goal before you sleep on the 30th.
Keep the rules for one more week.
